extracted.intended_audience: Programmers writing Singular scripts, procedures, and libraries (Singular users and library authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and formal rules for writing and organizing Singular commands, procedures, and libraries: syntax for declarations/assignments/prints, naming and typing rules, I/O (links), procedure parameter/help conventions, and library header/packaging requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: General command syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: In Singular a command is either a declaration, an assignment, a call to a function without return value, or a print command. The general form of a command is described in subsections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands take forms such as: declaration (type name = expression;), assignment (name = expression;), function calls without return, and print commands (expression;). Use semicolons to terminate statements. See specific subsections for details and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration syntax includes: 1) type name = expression ; 2) alias type name 3) type name list = expression list ; 4) type name ; Each declares variables and optionally assigns initial values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expression must be of the specified type or convertible to it (see type conversion). alias introduces a read-only alternative name and may only be used in procedure headings to avoid copying large data. In list declarations both name list and expression list must have same length. 'type name;' declares variable with default value of that type. Refer to Section 3.5.5 for conversions/casts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment uses 'name = expression ;' or 'name list = expression list ;'. Assignments convert RHS to LHS type if possible. Assignments are not expressions themselves and do not yield a value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigning lists is not simultaneous: f, g = g, f; assigns g to both f and g (not swap). Compound assignments like i = j = k; are not allowed and result in an error. Type conversion from the expression type to the name's type must be possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions without return value
rubrics_metrics.description: Function calls that have no return value are written as 'function name[(argument list)] ;'. Such functions can still produce output but their return type is 'none'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some functions must be called without parentheses (e.g., help, LIB). Distinguish between printed output and a typed return value. See Section 5.1 for function specifications. Example: degree(i); prints output without returning a typed value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print command and pretty output
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing 'expression ;' prints the value of an expression. For nicely formatted output use the print function (or show from inout.lib).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use print for matrices, intmat, etc. Example: int i=2; i; prints '2'. For structured types use print(m) to get readable presentation. See Section 5.1.117 [print].

rubrics_metrics.name: Special characters and operators (meanings)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of characters and operators have special meanings (assignment, parentheses, access operator, arithmetic ops, comparison ops, boolean ops, string delimiters, comment delimiters, statement separator, escape character, interval specifier, package member accessor, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of distinctions such as '/' vs div (see Section 6.4), '%' (or mod) yields non-negative result, '^' or '**' for exponentiation, '[]' for indexing/access, '//' and '/* */' comment delimiters, ',' separates expression lists, '..' interval specifier (1..3 -> intvec). Use '::' to access package members. A full mapping is provided in the manual; consult it to avoid syntactic mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names: declaration before use and redeclaration rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular is strongly typed: all names (identifiers) must be declared prior to use. It is possible to redefine an existing name only if doing so does not change its type; redefinition first sets the variable to the default value then computes the expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redeclaration vs overriding differs: 'int i=3; i=i+1;' overrides; 'int i=i+1;' is redefinition and sets default then computes expression, leading to different result. Use type() and attrib() to inspect names. Use listvar to list names in use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming conventions and allowed characters
rubrics_metrics.description: User-defined names should start with a letter and consist only of letters and digits. Exceptions: '@' and '_' may be used (with @ as first letter reserved for library routines). Names are case-sensitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid interference with ring variable names or monomials (see Section 6.5). Use reservedName() to list keywords that must not be used as names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexed names and multi-index construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexed names are built as name followed by an int expression in parentheses. A list of indexed names can be built with an intvec expression in parentheses. Multi-indices can be appended by another int expression in parentheses or via name_prefix(index1,index2,...) where name_prefix must be an undeclared name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ideal j(3) and ideal j(n) are equivalent if n==3. You can reference ranges like j(2..3). Ring variable declarations may use multi-level indexed names as shown in examples. Understand equivalences to avoid subtle bugs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserved names and avoiding name conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Names must not coincide with reserved names (keywords). Names should not interfere with ring variables or monomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reservedName() to obtain reserved names. Avoid naming that collides with ring variables; check Section 6.5 for identifier resolution issues. Use listvar to inspect current names in session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special name '_' and name substitution with backticks
rubrics_metrics.description: The most recently printed expression is available under the special name '_'. A string expression enclosed in backticks (‘...‘) evaluates to the value of the variable whose name is given by the string expression (name substitution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: after std(i); _[1] gives first generator; assign ideal k=_; and then operate on k. For name substitution: string bar="foo"; ‘bar+"(1)"‘ evaluates foo(1). Useful for dynamic references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects and ring locality
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects in Singular have types and values; many object types (poly, ideal, vector, module, map, matrix, number, resolution, and lists containing ring objects) belong to a specific ring and are local to that ring. Other types do not belong to a ring and are accessible across rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ring-local objects may be duplicated in different rings. To move objects between rings use maps, fetch, or imap. Be mindful of ring locality when manipulating polynomials/ideals and when killing or changing basering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type conversion in expressions and assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments convert the type of the RHS to the type of the LHS if possible. Operators and functions that require certain operand types may implicitly convert expression types. Type conversions do not act transitively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: multiplying a polynomial by an integer implicitly converts the integer to a polynomial. The manual lists possible conversions between types (intvec, poly, bigint, int, intmat, ideal, module, number, vector, matrix, list, resolution, string, etc.). Understand allowed conversions to avoid type errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type casting syntax and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit casting uses 'type(expression)'. Many casts are supported (to matrix, module, number, poly, ring, string, etc.). There are two forms to convert to a matrix: matrix(expression) infers size; matrix(expression,m,n) returns an m×n matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the provided mapping of from/to casts for valid casts. Examples: number(3x) -> 0, number(poly(3)) -> 3. matrix(i,3,2) reshapes ideal/list into given dimensions; module(matrix(...)) makes module with generators as columns. Some casts are inverses (e.g., ringlist <-> list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow control and blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: A block is a sequence of commands surrounded by { } and is used as the unit for structured programming. if/else structures and for/while loops execute blocks conditionally or repeatedly. Procedure main and example sections are also blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use braces to group sequences of commands. Examples: procedure bodies, main sections, and example sections must be enclosed in { }.

rubrics_metrics.name: I/O via links and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular I/O uses links (communication channels) which Singular can write to and read from (functions write/read). Monitoring (monitor command) makes a typescript of everything printed to a file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links can often be specified by filename strings and need not be explicitly opened; however open/close are available. Dump/getdump store or retrieve entire sessions to/from links (not available for DBM links). Use monitor to record sessions; use status(link,"open") to query link properties. Use execute(read(...)) to treat file content as code.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASCII, ssi, and DBM links: recommended uses
rubrics_metrics.description: ASCII links: plain text storage/communication, return strings on read; Ssi links: TCP/IP communication with other Singular processes (not a string, returns expressions) and suited for parallel computations; DBM links: key-value storage where both key and value are strings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ASCII links for small, inspectable data and interoperability; use ssi links for interprocess communication and parallelization (open(l) may launch a server); use DBM links for associative storage where conversion to/from strings is possible. Examples and usage patterns are shown in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure definition (syntax and metadata)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure syntax: [static] proc proc_name[(<parameter list>)] [<help string>] { <procedure body> } [example { <sequence of commands> }]. Help string, parameter list, and example are optional, but are mandatory for procedures listed in a library header.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help strings are ignored and example sections disallowed for interactively defined procedures (not loaded from file). When loaded from a file, help is shown by 'help proc_name;' and example executed by 'example proc_name;'. Procedures not meant for users should be declared static (especially inside libraries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter list rules and optional arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Parameter lists define the number, type, and names of arguments. The default parameter list is (list #) which allows optional parameters. Adding 'list #' as an argument allows optional parameters; inside the procedure, optional args are referenced as #[1], #[2], etc. size(#) gives number of optional args.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use attrib(proc,"default_arg",...) to set default values. If a parameter is of type ring, it may only be specified by name (e.g., proc x6(r) is correct; proc x7(ring r) is NOT correct). Parameter may be any type including proc and ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help string format for procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Help string is a string constant constituting the procedure's help text. Format should include lines such as USAGE:, ASSUME:, RETURN:, SIDE EFFECTS:, REMARKS:, NOTE:, KEYWORDS:, SEE ALSO:, EXAMPLE: and additional details. ASSUME, SIDE EFFECTS, KEYWORDS, and SEE ALSO are optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No help string is required for static procedures. EXAMPLE: refers to the example section; examples are executed upon 'example proc_name;' when loaded from file. Keep help strings readable; see typesetting section for texinfo considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names and variable scope within procedures; exporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables defined inside a procedure are local to it and are automatically deleted after leaving the procedure. To keep local variables and their values after leaving the procedure, export or exportto must be used. Use return to return a value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: proc xxx { int k=4; int result=k+2; export(result); } After calling xxx(), result will be global. Use export/exportto/importfrom appropriately when interacting with global state. Local names cannot interfere with names in other procedures unless exported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure-only commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain commands should be used only inside procedures because they make local objects global or return results to the caller (e.g., export, exportto, return).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These commands are intended to manage scope and return values from procedures; use them according to Section references for correct behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library structure and header requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A library is a file of Singular procedures. The first line must start with '//'. The header must include mandatory version, category, and info strings; LIB commands in header load additional libraries used. The library body contains procedures (static or not). No line in a library should exceed 60 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Info string is used for documentation generation and help libname.lib; it must follow a specific format (LIBRARY:, AUTHOR:, OVERVIEW:, REFERENCES:, KEYWORDS:, SEE ALSO:, PROCEDURES:). Only non-static procedures should be listed in PROCEDURES:. The version string syntax and category string are expected in header; adhere to exact formats to ensure proper parsing.

rubrics_metrics.name: LIB commands syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: LIB commands in the library header have syntax LIB "libname.lib"; and are used to load libraries required by the current library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The keyword LIB must be followed by at least one space. Example: LIB "primdec.lib"; LIB "normal.lib"; Use LIB commands to specify dependencies in the header so they are available when library is loaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Info string format and documentation generation
rubrics_metrics.description: The info string in a library header constitutes the help text of the library and must follow a prescribed format (LIBRARY: <name> <one line description>, AUTHORS:, OVERVIEW:, REFERENCES:, KEYWORDS:, SEE ALSO:, PROCEDURES: with one-line descriptions of procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Info strings are parsed and translated to texinfo for documentation; only non-static procedures should appear in PROCEDURES: since separate documentation nodes are created for these. Keep info/help texts verbatim-readable and concise; examples listed in PROCEDURES: are computed and included in docs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures in a library: implementation and style guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Hints/requirements: 1) declare non-user procedures static; 2) non-static procedures must have help & example sections and explain assumptions (use ERROR to report runtime assumption failures); 3) procedure names should be at least 4 characters, avoid special characters and underscore, and use CamelCase for multi-word names (e.g., linearMapKernel); 4) do not define procedures within other procedures; 5) control printed output using dbprint and global variable printlevel and internal variable voice; echo controls input echoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print behavior: use dbprint to conditionally display messages depending on printlevel and voice (voice reflects nesting level). Default printlevel is 0; echo default 0, input echoed if echo>=voice. Examples show saving/restoring printlevel and setting echo=2 during example sections. Follow these rules to make libraries robust when called from other procedures and for clean documentation output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typesetting and texinfo for library/help strings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Singular documentation uses texinfo. Info and help strings of libraries distributed with Singular are parsed and translated to texinfo format, and help strings of procedures listed in PROCEDURE: are included in documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep help/info texts readable verbatim (avoid excessive texinfo markup unless necessary). The example of each procedure listed in the PROCEDURE: section is computed and its output included in the documentation. See the typesetting section for specifics.
